activities.caption: pair each Baroque engine with the job it does
activities.name: mhBaroqueMatch

config.prompt: The Baroque sound-world — pair each device with its job:

pairs.right: bass line plus chordal partner, improvising the accompaniment from figures
the full orchestra's catchy tutti returns like a refrain between solo episodes
gut strings, natural trumpets, terraced dynamics, ornamentation the performer adds

config.why: Vivaldi's Spring shows the ritornello engine; Handel's Op. 6 the concerto grosso — the era's two competing dramatic engines.

activities.anchor: the basso continuo is just a harpsichord playing chords
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the continuo myth
activities.name: mhContinuoSpot

config.prompt: A programme note contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: The basso continuo underpins nearly all Baroque ensemble music, from opera recitative to concerto.
It is a partnership of at least two players: a bass instrument and a chordal instrument.
The chordal player reads fully written-out chords from the score.
Miss it and the texture's motor — the reason Baroque music moves the way it does — disappears.
config.correction: The chordal instrument realises the harmony un-notated, improvising from figures in real time.
config.why: The continuo is also the clearest audible marker distinguishing a historically informed performance from a modern-orchestra one.

activities.caption: drag the divider — density versus clarity
activities.name: mhEraCompare

config.prompt: Around 1750 — drag the divider between the two sound-worlds:

before.label: Baroque
before.text: Motor rhythm, one affect per movement, terraced dynamics (loud tutti, quiet solos, few graduations), the continuo's improvising engine.

after.label: Classical
after.text: Periodic phrasing — two- and four-bar questions answered — gradual crescendo on the flexing early pianoforte, sonata form as the great engine.

config.why: The social setting changed with the style: the public concert emerged, and music left the court chamber for ticket-buying audiences.

activities.anchor: one continuous movement following the river from its two springs
activities.caption: follow Vltava downstream
activities.name: mhVltavaOrder

config.prompt: Smetana's Vltava, the second of six symphonic poems in Má vlast, follows the river — order the journey:
items: A rustic wedding with a polka
The broad theme opens out — and the closing bars quote the Vyšehrad motif
config.why: One continuous orchestral movement following the river downstream — the episodes really do follow the water, and the closing bars tie it to Prague's fortress rock.

activities.anchor: nationalist music means quoting folk songs
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the Czech sound
activities.name: mhFolkPredict

config.q: Some Czech critics complained that Smetana used no genuine folk material. Why does Vltava still sound Czech?
choices: It quotes a hidden Czech hymn
Original folk-like themes, Czech titles and polka rhythms do the national work
config.why: Romantic nationalism was usually a style of musical behaviour — dances, modes, landscape painting, patriotic programmes — not a library of borrowed melodies. Vltava sounds Czech without quoting a single Czech tune.

activities.anchor: programme music tells the story in order
activities.caption: true or false — reading a programme
activities.name: mhProgrammeJudge

statements.why: They set the mood and justify the structure — a listener who has never read either programme can still hear the form.

statements.s: Vltava's episodes really do follow the river downstream.
statements.why: Though Symphonie fantastique's programme was revised and partly abandoned by Berlioz.

statements.s: The exam skill is guessing the narrative.
statements.why: It is describing the musical means — rhythm, orchestral colour, key, texture — that create the effect.

statements.s: Film scores are programme music by descent.
statements.why: The genre ran on through Richard Strauss's tone poems into the twentieth century's film scores.

activities.anchor: The textbook dates are conventions, and the edges are famously soft
activities.caption: scrub the era boundaries — signposts, not walls
activities.name: mhErasTimeline

events.title: Baroque begins (roughly)
events.text: The birth of opera and the orchestra — ornamented, rhythmic drive, the continuo engine.

events.title: The Classical door
events.text: Handel and Bach died in the 1750s still writing Baroque music while the galant style circled them.

events.title: Romantic (roughly)
events.text: Beethoven's career spans both sides of the Classical door and opened the Romantic one — the Eroica (1804) is claimed by both eras.

events.title: The 20th century
events.text: Schoenberg's atonality, Stravinsky's Rite (1913 riot), jazz, electronics, minimalism — 'classical' becomes one genre among many.

config.why: Treat the dates as signposts toward clusters of features — continuo, texture, dynamics, form, instrumentation — not as walls; examiners reward feature-spotting over date-reciting.
